# tritonctl instance

Manage instances (VMs)

Alias: inst

Subcommands: list, show, create, delete, start, stop, reboot, nics, disks, tags, logs

Usage: `tritonctl instance [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl instance list

List your instances

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl instance list [OPTIONS]`

- `--image <IMAGE>`: Only instances from this image (name, name@version, uuid, or prefix)
- `--state <STATE>`: Only instances in this lifecycle state (one of: pending, provisioning, running, stopping, stopped, deleting, failed)

## tritonctl instance show

Show one instance

Usage: `tritonctl instance show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl instance create

Create an instance in the project

Usage: `tritonctl instance create [OPTIONS] --name <NAME> --image <IMAGE> --subnet <SUBNET>`

- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--image <IMAGE>`: Image to boot (name, name@version, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--subnet <SUBNET>`: Subnet for the primary NIC (name, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--ssh-key <KEY>`: SSH key to install (name, fingerprint, uuid, or prefix). Repeatable
- `--package <PACKAGE>`: Size it from a package (name, name@version, uuid, or prefix) instead of --cpu and --memory. The package's default disks apply unless a --disk names its own
- `--cpu <CPU>`: Virtual CPUs. Needed without --package
- `--memory <SIZE>`: Memory: `4G`, `512M`, or bytes. Needed without --package
- `--disk <SPEC>`: A disk. Repeatable: `boot,type=replicated[,replicas=N][,tier=T]` puts the boot disk on replicated storage; `size=100G,type=replicated[,replicas=N][,tier=T]` adds a data disk; a bare `50G` sizes the boot disk
- `--tag <KEY=VALUE>`: A tag, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--data-disk <SIZE[,replicas=N][,tier=T]>`: A data disk replicated to other compute nodes: `100G`, with optional `,replicas=2` (3 by default) and `,tier=standard` (`performance` by default). The same as `--disk size=SIZE,type=replicated,...`. Repeatable
- `--user-data <FILE>`: cloud-init user data: a file path, or `-` for stdin
- `--wait`: Wait until the change has taken effect, then print the instance. Progress goes to stderr; gives up after 15 minutes

## tritonctl instance delete

Delete an instance. It must be stopped or failed

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl instance delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix
- `--force`: Delete an instance that is not stopped or failed. The server still decides
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
- `--wait`: Wait until the change has taken effect, then print the instance. Progress goes to stderr; gives up after 15 minutes

## tritonctl instance start

Start an instance

Usage: `tritonctl instance start [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix
- `--wait`: Wait until the change has taken effect, then print the instance. Progress goes to stderr; gives up after 15 minutes

Usage: `tritonctl instance stop [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix
- `--wait`: Wait until the change has taken effect, then print the instance. Progress goes to stderr; gives up after 15 minutes

Reboot an instance

Usage: `tritonctl instance reboot [OPTIONS] <ID>`

## tritonctl instance nics

List an instance's NICs

Usage: `tritonctl instance nics [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl instance disks

List an instance's disks

Usage: `tritonctl instance disks [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl instance tags

Show an instance's tags, or change them

Usage: `tritonctl instance tags [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix
- `--set <KEY=VALUE>`: Set a tag, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--unset <KEY>`: Remove a tag. Repeatable
- `--replace`: Remove every tag not set here

## tritonctl instance logs

Print the tail of an instance's log

Usage: `tritonctl instance logs [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix
- `--source <SOURCE>`: Which log: `console` (the guest's) or `platform` (default: console)
- `--lines <LINES>`: How many lines from the end (default: 100)
